source: NCERT Class XII, India — People and Economy, Ch. 2 (Migration: Types, Causes and Consequences).

sections.heading: 1. Migration — Types
points: **Migration** = the movement of people from one place to another to live/work.
**Internal migration** (within a country) — four streams: **rural-to-rural, rural-to-urban, urban-to-urban, urban-to-rural**.
**International migration** — **immigration (in)** and **emigration (out)**; India has both (a large diaspora abroad, and immigrants from neighbours).
In India, **rural-to-rural** is the largest stream; **females migrate mostly for marriage**, **males for work/employment**.

sections.heading: 2. Causes of Migration
points: **Push factors** — force people to leave: poverty, unemployment, poor conditions, disasters, conflict.
**Pull factors** — attract people to a place: jobs, better wages, education, health, security, city life.
In India, the main reason for migration is **work/employment (men)** and **marriage (women)**.

sections.heading: 3. Consequences of Migration
points: **Economic:** remittances (money sent home) aid source areas; but 'brain drain' (loss of skilled people).
**Demographic:** redistribution of population; urban growth; imbalance of age/sex at source and destination.
**Social:** intermixing of cultures; but also anonymity, slums, and social tension.
**Environmental:** overcrowding, pressure on urban infrastructure and resources.

sections.heading: 4. Migration and the Indian Diaspora
points: India has a large **diaspora** (overseas Indians) — a major source of remittances and soft power.
Historical migration (indentured labour) and modern skilled migration (to the Gulf, USA, UK).
Migration is a key factor shaping India's population and economy.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Internal streams: rural-rural (largest in India), rural-urban, urban-urban, urban-rural.
Push factors (drive out) vs pull factors (attract).
In India: men migrate mainly for work, women mainly for marriage.
Consequences: remittances, brain drain, urban slums, cultural mixing.
India has a large diaspora (major remittance source).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: In India, the **largest migration stream is rural-to-rural**.
**Women migrate mainly for marriage; men mainly for work**.
**Push factors drive people out; pull factors attract** them.
**Emigration = leaving a country; immigration = entering** one.
